To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the key barriers to appropriate polypharmacy were identified and mapped on to behaviour change techniques that could be used to overcome these barriers.

the key theoretical domains that are perceived to influence the appropriate prescribing and dispensing to older people in primary are: ‘Skills’, Beliefs about capabilities’, Beliefs about consequences’, Environmental context and resources’, Memory, attention and decision’, Social/professional role’, Social influences’, Behavioural regulation’.

the most important barriers and enablers to improving appropriate polypharmacy were related to the skills, knowledge and attitudes of GPs and pharmacists, and that the most promising intervention techniques to overcome these barriers are those that encourage GPs and pharmacrists to plan and review their behaviour, and those that provide prompts or reminders.

identifying and addressing barriers and facilitators in order to improve appropriate poly-pharmacy for older people and will inform the design and delivery of future intervention studies.

the development of an intervention to support GPs and community pharmacists in the prescribing and dispens of appropriate polyphrapy to older patients.

the use of theory to guide intervention design is a valuable approach to improving appropriate polypharmacy.
